# Terraform AWS CloudWatch Observability Setup Module

 [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup/commits)


Configure opt-in account/Region CloudWatch observability settings with the
HashiCorp AWS and AWS Cloud Control (AWSCC) Terraform providers. The module
covers Application Signals, X-Ray Transaction Search and trace controls,
Observability Admin account telemetry, CloudWatch Logs account policies and
log groups, and an optional KMS key that encrypts log groups, X-Ray traces,
and Transaction Search spans.


---

This project is part of our comprehensive approach towards DevOps Acceleration.

## Introduction

This module manages **account/Region settings**, not workload instrumentation.
The optional `cloudwatch` input defaults to `{}` and creates no resources.
Deploy at most one instance of this module per AWS account and
Region (preferably in a shared or hub stack). Enable only settings this
Terraform state should own. Inventory and import existing singleton settings
before enabling them; two states must not own one setting. CloudWatch Logs
resource/account policies and X-Ray encryption use create-or-update APIs,
so applying a duplicate owner can overwrite existing settings instead of
failing safely.

| Capability | Terraform ownership | Input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application Signals discovery (creates the `AWSServiceRoleForCloudWatchApplicationSignals` service-linked role) and grouping | `awscc_applicationsignals_discovery`, `awscc_applicationsignals_grouping_configuration` | `cloudwatch.application_signals` |
| X-Ray Transaction Search (span ingestion and trace indexing rate), which also turns on Application Signals discovery | `awscc_xray_transaction_search_config`, preceded by `aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy` | `cloudwatch.application_signals.ingest_otel_spans` / `trace_indexing_rate`; advanced settings in `cloudwatch.transaction_search` |
| X-Ray trace encryption, groups, sampling | `aws_xray_encryption_config`, `aws_xray_group`, `aws_xray_sampling_rule` | `cloudwatch.xray` |
| Account telemetry inventory and tag enrichment | `aws_observabilityadmin_telemetry_evaluation`, `aws_observabilityadmin_telemetry_enrichment` | `cloudwatch.telemetry` |
| CloudWatch Logs account policies | `aws_cloudwatch_log_account_policy` | `cloudwatch.log_account_policies` |
| CloudWatch Logs log groups | `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` | `cloudwatch.log_groups` |
| KMS encryption for log groups, X-Ray traces, and `aws/spans` | `aws_kms_key`, `aws_kms_alias`, attachable `aws_iam_policy` | `cloudwatch.encryption` |

AWSCC owns Transaction Search indexing/destination. **Do not also manage**
`aws_xray_indexing_rule` or `aws_xray_trace_segment_destination` in the same
account/Region. X-Ray sampling is separate from indexing. The module creates
the scoped Logs resource policy for `aws/spans` and
`/aws/application-signals/data` before Transaction Search. The
indexing rate (`trace_indexing_rate` or `indexing_percentage`) is **0–100 percent**, not a fraction. See
[AWS Transaction Search setup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Transaction-Search-Cloudformation.html)
and [the configuration reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-xray-transactionsearchconfig.html).

Application Signals discovery enables account integration and creates the
`AWSServiceRoleForCloudWatchApplicationSignals` service-linked role; it does
not install collectors or instrument workloads. Grouping owns one
whole-account configuration. Older discovery may require a separate
Application Map migration. See
[Application Signals discovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-applicationsignals-discovery.html).

**Transaction Search and Application Signals**

The two Transaction Search settings on the CloudWatch Application Signals
console page are inputs under `application_signals`:

| Console setting | Input | AWS effect | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ingest OpenTelemetry spans | `ingest_otel_spans` | X-Ray sends spans to the `aws/spans` log group as structured logs (Transaction Search) | Off, unless a `transaction_search` block is set |
| Trace indexing rate | `trace_indexing_rate` | Percentage of ingested spans indexed as trace summaries, 0–100 | `1` (the included tier) |

`cloudwatch.transaction_search` holds the advanced settings (`policy_name`,
`spans_encryption`, `import_existing`). Its `enabled` and
`indexing_percentage` are the same AWS settings as `ingest_otel_spans` and
`trace_indexing_rate`, kept for v1.0.0 inputs: `enabled` must not disagree
with `ingest_otel_spans`, and only one of the two rates may be set. A
`transaction_search` block without either switch still enables ingestion,
as in v1.0.0; with `ingest_otel_spans` set, the block follows it.

Ingesting spans also turns on Application Signals discovery, so the
service-linked role exists and Application Signals can use the spans. AWS
starts discovery whenever it enables Transaction Search, so the module
manages discovery whenever `application_signals.enabled` or span ingestion
is on, and creates discovery first.

| Turning off | Effect in AWS |
| --- | --- |
| Span ingestion (`ingest_otel_spans: false`) | X-Ray stops sending spans to CloudWatch Logs. `aws/spans` and its data remain. |
| Discovery (both flags `false`) | The resource leaves state. Application Signals has no operation that stops discovery, so the account stays enabled and the service-linked role remains. Re-enabling later needs `application_signals.import_existing: true`; once discovery has ever been on, that flag can stay set permanently. |

**Adopting existing settings (`import_existing`)**

Discovery and Transaction Search are account singletons. Their create fails
when they are already enabled, for example from the console, an earlier
Transaction Search enablement, or another stack (AWS asks that
[Transaction Search be disabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Transaction-Search-Cloudformation.html)
before infrastructure as code enables it). Set `import_existing: true` on the
setting instead, and the module imports it by account ID on the next plan:

| Already enabled in the account | Set |
| --- | --- |
| Application Signals discovery | `application_signals.import_existing: true` |
| Transaction Search (discovery is almost always on too) | `transaction_search.import_existing: true` and `application_signals.import_existing: true` |

- The plan shows `will be imported`. Once imported, the flag is a no-op and can stay set. Clear `transaction_search.import_existing` before turning span ingestion off, because a later re-enable would otherwise try to import a disabled setting.
- Set `trace_indexing_rate` to the account's current value (`aws xray get-indexing-rules`) before importing; otherwise the same apply also changes it. Read the update lines in the plan, not only `will be imported`.
- Set both flags when Transaction Search is already on. With only `transaction_search.import_existing`, the discovery create fails as already existing and the Transaction Search import is not saved until both are set.
- Set a flag only when the setting exists: importing a setting that is not enabled fails the plan with `Cannot import non-existent remote object`. Check with `aws xray get-trace-segment-destination` (`Destination: CloudWatchLogs` means Transaction Search is enabled) and `aws iam get-role --role-name AWSServiceRoleForCloudWatchApplicationSignals` (the role exists once discovery has been started).
- An imported Transaction Search keeps its current `aws/spans` encryption; `spans_encryption` and the module key apply only when this state first enables it.
- The module's Logs resource policy (`policy_name`) is written with a create-or-update API and does not need importing. The console may have created a second, differently named policy; remove it only after confirming this module's policy is in place.
- Import blocks require Terraform or OpenTofu `>= 1.7` and work only in a root module. Terragrunt deploys this module as the root module; calling it with a `module` block from another configuration is not supported.
- Destroying an adopted Transaction Search turns it off, as for one the module created.

**Encryption**

`cloudwatch.encryption.enabled: true` creates a symmetric KMS key with
automatic rotation always on, an alias, and an attachable IAM policy. The
alias defaults to `alias/<system_name>-observability`, where `<system_name>`
is `<org unit>-<environment name>-<environment type>-<spoke>-<region code>`,
for example `devops-prod-production-001-usea1`. IAM policy names are
account-wide and short Region codes can collide (`ap-south-1` and
`ap-southeast-1` both shorten to `apso1`), so the policy name defaults to the
full Region name, for example
`devops-prod-production-001-us-east-1-observability-encryption`. The module
applies the key to every target that has no local override:

| Target | Module key applied to | Local override |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module log groups | `kms_key_id` of each `cloudwatch.log_groups` entry | `log_groups.<name>.encryption`: `type: NONE` keeps CloudWatch Logs default encryption; `type: KMS` with a key ARN uses that key |
| X-Ray traces | `aws_xray_encryption_config` with `type: KMS` | `xray.encryption` |
| Transaction Search spans (`aws/spans`) | `spans_log_group_kms_key_id`, **only when Transaction Search is first enabled** | `transaction_search.spans_encryption` |
| Transaction Search `/aws/application-signals/data` | Only when declared in `cloudwatch.log_groups` (see below) | That entry's `encryption` |

With encryption enabled, this state always owns the account/Region X-Ray
encryption setting, either with the module key or with your `xray.encryption`
override; it cannot leave X-Ray encryption to another owner.

The key policy keeps the account-root statement, so IAM policies in the
account can grant use of the key, and lets the Regional CloudWatch Logs
service principal use it only for log groups in this account and Region.
CloudWatch Logs requires every role that writes to or reads from an
encrypted log group to hold key permissions through `kms:ViaService`. Attach
the `encryption_policy_arn` output to those roles, for example Lambda
execution roles, ECS task execution roles (`awslogs` driver) or task roles
(FireLens), CloudWatch agent or ADOT collector roles, and flow-log delivery
roles. The policy grants key use through CloudWatch Logs, plus
`kms:Decrypt` through X-Ray for roles that read encrypted traces. Trace
writers need no key permission, because X-Ray encrypts through the grant
created when its encryption is configured. The policy grants no `logs:` or
`xray:` actions, so keep each role's existing logging and tracing policies.
See [CloudWatch Logs KMS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/encrypt-log-data-kms.html)
and [X-Ray data protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-console-encryption.html).

X-Ray sets the `aws/spans` key only while it creates that log group during
Transaction Search enablement, and the key must be a key ARN in this account
and Region. Changing it afterwards replaces the configuration, which fails
while Transaction Search is on, so the module ignores later changes. Two
cases need the key associated once by hand (this needs
`logs:AssociateKmsKey`), with
`aws logs associate-kms-key --log-group-name aws/spans --kms-key-id <kms_key_arn>`:

- Transaction Search was already enabled before encryption was turned on,
  whether by this state or outside Terraform and then imported. The plan
  leaves `aws/spans` unchanged.
- `aws/spans` already exists while Transaction Search is being enabled, for
  example after an earlier enablement. A keyed enablement fails here, so set
  `transaction_search.spans_encryption.type: NONE` first.

The spans key covers only `aws/spans`. To encrypt
`/aws/application-signals/data` as well, declare it in `cloudwatch.log_groups`
before Transaction Search is first enabled. The module creates its log groups
before it enables Transaction Search, so the group gets the module key or its
own override. If the log group already exists, adopt it as described below
and the key is associated in place for newly ingested data. See
[Transaction Search encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Enable-TransactionSearch.html#Enable-TransactionSearch-kms).

**Log groups**

`cloudwatch.log_groups` is keyed by log group name; names cannot start with
`aws/`. Creating a log group that already exists fails. To adopt one, declare
it in `log_groups` with its current retention, class, key (`encryption`
override), deletion protection, and tags; import it before the first apply
with `terragrunt import 'aws_cloudwatch_log_group.this["/app/checkout"]' /app/checkout`;
and review the plan. Unset settings are reconciled to module values: a null
`retention_in_days` removes the retention policy (never expire), and a group
without an `encryption` override moves to the module key, or to default
encryption when module encryption is off. `deletion_protection_enabled`
defaults to null, which keeps the current setting; new log groups are created
without protection. `log_group_class` is set at
creation only and later changes are ignored: AWS cannot change a class, so a
diff would replace the log group and delete its data. AWS also starts
reporting `INFREQUENT_ACCESS` log groups as `ESSENTIALS` in December 2026
([log classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CloudWatch_Logs_Log_Classes.html)).
The `DELIVERY` class is only for Lambda logs delivered to Amazon S3 or Amazon
Data Firehose and keeps events for a fixed, short period.

**Prerequisites and limits**

- Terraform or OpenTofu `>= 1.7` (for conditional `import` blocks), AWS provider `>= 6.69.0, < 7.0.0`, AWSCC provider `>= 1.108.0, < 2.0.0` (the first AWSCC release with the `aws/spans` key setting). Deployments whose lock file pins an older AWSCC must run `terragrunt init -upgrade`. Configure both providers for the same account and Region in the caller; do not let AWSCC silently fall back to different ambient credentials.
- Grant the caller the relevant CloudWatch Logs, X-Ray, Application Signals, Observability Admin, and Cloud Control API permissions for enabled settings. Discovery and Transaction Search create the Application Signals service-linked role, so the caller needs `iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole` and `application-signals:StartDiscovery`.
- **Upgrading from v1.0.0:** the module now needs Terraform or OpenTofu `>= 1.7` and must be the root module (as under Terragrunt). With `transaction_search` set and `application_signals.enabled: false`: the next plan adds discovery, which AWS already enabled with Transaction Search. Set `application_signals.import_existing: true` for that apply so discovery is imported instead of failing to create.
- Do not enable account `telemetry.evaluation` where AWS Organizations already manages telemetry evaluation. Creation may succeed while destruction is rejected. Organization-level setup is outside this module. See [the AWS provider warning](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/observabilityadmin_telemetry_evaluation) and [AWS organization setup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/telemetry-config-turn-on.html).
- X-Ray `encryption` configures traces, **not** the CloudWatch Logs `aws/spans` group; `aws/spans` follows `transaction_search.spans_encryption` as described in **Encryption**. The AWS provider accepts only an ARN (key or alias ARN) for `xray.encryption.key_id`. Destroying `aws_xray_encryption_config` does not reset the service setting: apply `type: NONE` before removing the input if you intend to revert KMS encryption. See [X-Ray encryption config](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/xray_encryption_config).
- With `encryption.enabled`, the deploying principal also needs permission to create and manage the KMS key, alias, and IAM policy; `kms:DescribeKey` on every key it associates with a log group or `aws/spans`; and `kms:CreateGrant` plus `kms:DescribeKey` on the key used for X-Ray. X-Ray stops storing traces if the principal that configured its encryption loses access to the key, so keep the deploying role's key permissions in place.
- IAM cannot delete a policy that is still attached. Detach `encryption_policy_arn` from every role, and remove it from consumer stacks, before turning encryption off, destroying the module, or changing `iam_policy.name` or `iam_policy.path` (either change replaces the policy). Otherwise the apply stops partway.
- **Turning encryption off, or destroying the module, schedules the key for deletion** after `deletion_window_in_days` (default 30). A key pending deletion cannot be used: X-Ray stops storing traces while its setting still names the key, and log data already encrypted with the key, including `aws/spans` and log groups kept by `skip_destroy`, becomes unreadable. Data in never-expire log groups never ages out, so it becomes permanently unreadable once the key is deleted. To stop encrypting new data but keep existing data readable, leave `encryption.enabled: true` and set local `type: NONE` overrides. Before turning encryption off, set `xray.encryption.type: NONE`, disassociate the key from `aws/spans` and any retained log groups, and wait for data encrypted with the key to expire. Cancel an unintended deletion with `aws kms cancel-key-deletion`.
- Logs account-policy JSON and selection criteria are type-specific; `scope` currently accepts only `ALL`. The [current Logs API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_PutAccountPolicy.html) lists `METRIC_EXTRACTION_POLICY` in addition to the four types in the [AWS provider v6.71 documentation](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/blob/v6.71.0/website/docs/r/cloudwatch_log_account_policy.html.markdown), so verify provider support before using that newer type. A subscription-filter policy can export account-wide logs; a data-protection policy can incur per-GB scanning charges. A metric-extraction policy can suppress Application Signals metrics if it includes `/aws/application-signals/data`.
- Transaction Search includes indexing of 1% of ingested spans, but span ingestion is still billed; indexing above 1% can add cost. See [AWS Transaction Search setup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Enable-TransactionSearch.html) and [CloudWatch pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/pricing/). Enabling enrichment or other logging can also incur charges. A customer managed key adds a monthly key charge plus a charge for each request that CloudWatch Logs and X-Ray make to encrypt or decrypt data; see [AWS KMS pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/).

Workload instrumentation, dashboards, alarms, OAM links, and organization-wide
telemetry rules are separate deployments, not features of this module.

## Usage


**IMPORTANT:** The `master` branch is used in `source` just as an example. In your code, do not pin to `master` because there may be breaking changes between releases.
Instead pin to the release tag (e.g. `?ref=vX.Y.Z`) of one of our [latest releases](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup/releases).


Begin with the [Terragrunt scaffold](https://docs.terragrunt.com/reference/cli/commands/scaffold).
Create and enter the target directory first; scaffold writes `terragrunt.hcl`,
`inputs.yaml`, and `local-tags.json` into the current directory.

```sh
mkdir -p dev/us-east-1/shared/cloudwatch-observability
cd dev/us-east-1/shared/cloudwatch-observability
terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup
vi inputs.yaml
# Ensure the parent root.hcl configures both providers as shown below.
terragrunt plan
terragrunt apply
```

Scaffold resolves the latest release tag into a pinned `terraform.source`.
Use a release (or tested pre-release) tag that contains these scaffold fixes;
older published tags may still contain the prior template errors. Before
applying, configure both providers in the parent Terragrunt `root.hcl` with
the same Region, source profile, and target role. For example, set
`AWS_REGION`, `AWS_PROFILE`, and `OBSERVABILITY_ROLE_ARN` and use:

```hcl
generate "observability_providers" {
  path      = "observability-providers.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = <<-EOF
provider "aws" {
  region  = "${get_env("AWS_REGION")}"
  profile = "${get_env("AWS_PROFILE")}"
  assume_role {
    role_arn = "${get_env("OBSERVABILITY_ROLE_ARN")}"
  }
}

provider "awscc" {
  region  = "${get_env("AWS_REGION")}"
  profile = "${get_env("AWS_PROFILE")}"
  assume_role = {
    role_arn = "${get_env("OBSERVABILITY_ROLE_ARN")}"
  }
}
EOF
}
```

The AWS provider uses an `assume_role` block; AWSCC uses an
`assume_role` object. See the [AWS provider](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/blob/v6.71.0/website/docs/index.html.markdown)
and [AWSCC provider](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-awscc/blob/v1.108.0/docs/index.md)
configuration references. If your root stack already generates providers,
add AWSCC to that generator instead of creating a second provider file.

The Terragrunt hierarchy must provide `root.hcl`, `env-inputs.yaml`,
`global-inputs.yaml`, and `global-tags.json` in parent directories. The
scaffold creates `local-tags.json`. The `shared` directory is the single
logical owner for this account/Region, not an AWS isolation boundary. Choose
non-hub scaffold mode for the example below. Review the plan before changing
account-wide settings.

The generated `inputs.yaml` contains this module-specific key and annotated
option tree as comments. There is only one `cloudwatch` key in the generated
file, commented out by default, so the module uses its safe `{}` default.
Uncomment that key and replace the empty object only for settings this state
will own; the nested lines are illustrative comments, not a second key.

```yaml
#cloudwatch: {} # (Optional) Account/Region settings; default {} manages nothing.
#   application_signals: # (Optional) Discovery/grouping settings; default {}.
#     enabled: true # (Optional) Enable discovery, which creates the Application Signals service-linked role; default false; forced on while spans are ingested.
#     ingest_otel_spans: true # (Optional) Console "Ingest OpenTelemetry spans": send X-Ray spans to the aws/spans log group (Transaction Search); default null (off unless a transaction_search block is set).
#     trace_indexing_rate: 1 # (Optional) Console "Trace indexing rate": percent of ingested spans indexed, 0-100; default null (1, the included tier); exclusive with transaction_search.indexing_percentage.
#     import_existing: false # (Optional) Import discovery already enabled in this account instead of creating it; default false; fails if it does not exist; can stay set (discovery cannot be stopped).
#     grouping_attributes: # (Optional) Whole-account grouping configuration; default [].
#       - grouping_name: "Environment" # (Required) Name, 1-128 characters.
#         grouping_source_keys: ["deployment.environment"] # (Required) Nonempty list.
#         default_grouping_value: "unknown" # (Optional) Fallback, 1-128 characters; default null.
#   transaction_search: # (Optional) Advanced Transaction Search settings; the block alone also enables span ingestion (v1.0.0 behaviour); default null; use {} for all defaults (an empty key is null).
#     enabled: true # (Optional) Same switch as application_signals.ingest_otel_spans (must not disagree); default null (follows ingest_otel_spans, otherwise true).
#     indexing_percentage: 1 # (Optional) Same setting as application_signals.trace_indexing_rate (set only one), 0-100; default null (1).
#     policy_name: "CloudWatchTransactionSearch" # (Optional) Default shown.
#     import_existing: false # (Optional) Import Transaction Search already enabled in this account instead of creating it; default false; fails if it is not enabled; clear before turning ingestion off; match the indexing rate to the current value.
#     spans_encryption: # (Optional) aws/spans key override, applied only when Transaction Search is first enabled; default null (module key when encryption.enabled).
#       type: "KMS" # (Required) NONE (no key at creation) or KMS.
#       key_id: "arn:aws:kms:region:account:key/key-id" # (Optional) Key ARN in this account and Region, not an ID or alias; required for KMS.
#   xray: # (Optional) X-Ray encryption, groups, and sampling; default {}.
#     encryption: # (Optional) Trace encryption override; default null (module key when encryption.enabled, otherwise unmanaged).
#       type: "KMS" # (Required) NONE or KMS.
#       key_id: "arn:aws:kms:region:account:key/key-id" # (Optional) Required for KMS; default null.
#     groups: # (Optional) Map keyed by group name; default {}.
#       checkout: # (Optional) Example group.
#         filter_expression: 'service("checkout")' # (Required) X-Ray filter expression.
#         insights_enabled: true # (Optional) Default false.
#         notifications_enabled: false # (Optional) Default false.
#     sampling_rules: # (Optional) Map keyed by rule name; default {}.
#       checkout: # (Optional) Example rule.
#         fixed_rate: 0.1 # (Required) Fraction, 0-1.
#         priority: 100 # (Required) 1-9999.
#         reservoir_size: 1 # (Required) Nonnegative integer.
#         host: "*" # (Optional) Default "*".
#         http_method: "*" # (Optional) Default "*".
#         resource_arn: "*" # (Optional) Default "*".
#         service_name: "*" # (Optional) Default "*".
#         service_type: "*" # (Optional) Default "*".
#         url_path: "*" # (Optional) Default "*".
#         attributes: {} # (Optional) Default {}.
#   telemetry: # (Optional) Account Observability Admin settings; default {}.
#     evaluation: # (Optional) Account telemetry evaluation; default null.
#       all_regions: true # (Optional) Exclusive with regions; default null (current Region only).
#       # regions: ["us-east-1"] # (Optional) Exclusive with all_regions; default null (current Region only).
#     enrichment: true # (Optional) Default false.
#   log_account_policies: # (Optional) Map keyed by account policy name; default {}.
#     example: # (Optional) Example policy.
#       policy_document: '{"Fields":["requestId"]}' # (Required) Type-specific JSON.
#       policy_type: "FIELD_INDEX_POLICY" # (Required) AWS API types: DATA_PROTECTION_POLICY, SUBSCRIPTION_FILTER_POLICY, FIELD_INDEX_POLICY, TRANSFORMER_POLICY, METRIC_EXTRACTION_POLICY; verify provider support.
#       scope: "ALL" # (Optional) Only valid value is ALL; default ALL.
#       # selection_criteria: null # (Optional) Type-specific selector; default null; omit for this example.
#   log_groups: # (Optional) Map keyed by log group name (1-512 of a-z A-Z 0-9 . - _ / #, not starting with aws/); default {}.
#     /app/checkout: # (Optional) Example log group.
#       retention_in_days: 30 # (Optional) 0 (never expire), 1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 365, 400, 545, 731, 1096, 1827, 2192, 2557, 2922, 3288 or 3653; default null (never expire).
#       log_group_class: "STANDARD" # (Optional) STANDARD, INFREQUENT_ACCESS or DELIVERY; default STANDARD; set at creation only, later changes are ignored.
#       deletion_protection_enabled: true # (Optional) Block deletion until set to false; default null (keeps the current setting; new log groups are unprotected).
#       skip_destroy: false # (Optional) Keep the log group and its data on destroy; default false.
#       encryption: # (Optional) Module key override; default null (module key when encryption.enabled).
#         type: "KMS" # (Required) NONE (CloudWatch Logs default encryption) or KMS.
#         key_id: "arn:aws:kms:region:account:key/key-id" # (Optional) Key ARN, not an ID or alias; required for KMS.
#       tags: {} # (Optional) Extra tags for this log group; default {}.
#   encryption: # (Optional) Module KMS key for log groups, X-Ray, and aws/spans; default {} (disabled).
#     enabled: true # (Optional) Create the key, alias, and attachable IAM policy, and apply the key wherever no override is set; default false.
#     alias_name: "observability" # (Optional) Alias without the alias/ prefix, not starting with aws/; default "<system_name>-observability".
#     deletion_window_in_days: 30 # (Optional) Key deletion waiting period, 7-30 days; default 30.
#     rotation_period_in_days: 365 # (Optional) Rotation period (rotation is always on), 90-2560 days; default 365.
#     iam_policy: # (Optional) Attachable key-use policy for roles that write or read encrypted data; default {}.
#       name: "observability-encryption" # (Optional) Account-wide name, 1-128 of A-Z a-z 0-9 +=,.@_-; default "<org unit>-<env name>-<env type>-<spoke>-<region>-observability-encryption".
#       path: "/" # (Optional) IAM path up to 512 printable characters, no spaces, beginning and ending with /; default "/".
```

The corrected non-hub scaffold renders this `terragrunt.hcl` structure.
`terraform.source` is pinned to the release tag resolved by scaffold; replace
`vX.Y.Z` below with the tag containing these changes. The
`local.local_vars.cloudwatch` value maps to the module input.

```hcl
locals {
  local_vars  = yamldecode(file("./inputs.yaml"))
  env_vars    = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-inputs.yaml")))
  global_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-inputs.yaml")))
  global_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-tags.json")))
  local_tags  = jsondecode(file("./local-tags.json"))

  tags = merge(local.global_tags, local.local_tags)
}

include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}

terraform {
  source = "git::https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-observability-setup.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
}

inputs = {
  org        = local.env_vars.org
  cloudwatch = try(local.local_vars.cloudwatch, {})
  extra_tags = local.tags
}
```

## Quick Start

1. Configure AWS credentials and matching `aws` and `awscc` providers in the calling root stack, as shown in **Usage**.
2. Scaffold a deployment as shown in **Usage**; inspect `inputs.yaml` and `terragrunt.hcl`.
3. Leave `#cloudwatch: {}` commented for a no-op start; then uncomment it and enable one setting at a time. For discovery or Transaction Search already enabled in the account, set that setting's `import_existing: true`.
4. To encrypt, set `encryption.enabled: true` and attach the `encryption_policy_arn` output to every role that writes to or reads from encrypted log groups.
5. Run `terragrunt plan`, review account/Region changes and potential charges, then apply.


## Examples

### Application Signals and Transaction Search

Put this in `inputs.yaml` to enable Application Signals with span
ingestion and 1% trace indexing, and to set account grouping.

```yaml
cloudwatch:
  application_signals:
    enabled: true
    ingest_otel_spans: true
    trace_indexing_rate: 1
    grouping_attributes:
      - grouping_name: Environment
        grouping_source_keys: [deployment.environment]
        default_grouping_value: unknown
```

### Adopting settings enabled from the console

When Transaction Search and Application Signals are already on in the
account, import them instead of creating them. Keep the flags after the
first apply; they are no-ops once the settings are in state.

```yaml
cloudwatch:
  application_signals:
    enabled: true
    import_existing: true
    ingest_otel_spans: true
    trace_indexing_rate: 5   # the account's current rate
  transaction_search:
    import_existing: true
```

### X-Ray encryption, grouping, and sampling

Sampling is separate from Transaction Search indexing. `NONE` selects X-Ray's
service-managed trace encryption; use `KMS` with `key_id` only with a suitable
customer-managed key.

```yaml
cloudwatch:
  xray:
    encryption:
      type: NONE
    groups:
      checkout:
        filter_expression: 'service("checkout")'
        insights_enabled: true
    sampling_rules:
      checkout:
        fixed_rate: 0.1
        priority: 100
        reservoir_size: 1
```

### Encrypted log groups, traces, and spans

One switch encrypts the module log groups, X-Ray traces, and (on first
enablement) the Transaction Search `aws/spans` log group with the module key.
`/app/public` opts out locally and keeps CloudWatch Logs default encryption.

```yaml
cloudwatch:
  encryption:
    enabled: true
  application_signals:
    ingest_otel_spans: true
  log_groups:
    /app/checkout:
      retention_in_days: 90
    /app/audit:
      retention_in_days: 365
      deletion_protection_enabled: true
    /app/public:
      retention_in_days: 14
      encryption:
        type: NONE
```

Attach the key-use policy to each workload role that writes to or reads from
these log groups. For example, a workload stack can read the output through a
Terragrunt dependency and pass it to that module's managed-policy input (the
input name depends on the consuming module):

```hcl
dependency "observability" {
  config_path = "../../shared/cloudwatch-observability"
}

inputs = {
  extra_policy_arns = [dependency.observability.outputs.encryption_policy_arn]
}
```

### Account telemetry

Use only when AWS Organizations does not already own evaluation for the
account. `all_regions` and `regions` are mutually exclusive.

```yaml
cloudwatch:
  telemetry:
    evaluation:
      all_regions: true
    enrichment: true
```
